texts.facts: As per the prosecution, on 02.09.2000, Food Inspector Mr. Sureshchandra Nagar during his usual patrolling hours saw the petitioner on a motorcycle with a tank of milk. Thereafter, the Food Inspector asked the petitioner to produce his food license to [2025:RJ-JD:25182] (2 of 4) [CRLR-1143/2006] which the petitioner responded that he does not possess any Food License. The Food Inspector purchased 750 ml of milk from the petitioner and sent the same for examination to the Public Analyst. The Public Analyst in its report found that the milk samples were adulterated and there was presence of about 33% water in the said sample. On the basis of the report of the Public Analyst, the petitioner was prosecuted for the offence under Section 7/16 of the Act of 1954.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the sentence awarded to the petitioner has already been suspended by this Court vide order dated 13.12.2006 in Cr. Misc. Suspension of Sentence (Bail) No. 318/06. Jamalu Deen vs State (2025:Rj-Jd:25182) on 14 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62777084/ 1 Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that since there was a time gap of 7 months between the time when the samples were collected and the time when the complaint was lodged is fatal to the case of the prosecution. Furthermore, the counsel submitted that even though there was a huge crowd of people present when the sample was taken, the Food Inspector still called upon his subordinates to be the witness for the collection of the sample which puts a question upon his integrity and impartiality. In the alternative, he submitted that since the occurrence relates to year 2000 and the petitioner has already served some part of the sentence awarded to him, therefore, the substantive sentence awarded to the petitioner be reduced to the period already undergone by him. Reliance was placed on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Puttaswamy v State of Karnataka:2009 (1) WLC (SC) (Cri.) 623 and a [2025:RJ-JD:25182] (3 of 4) [CRLR-1143/2006] judgment of Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Kamla Prasad v. State of Rajasthan: 2014 CriLJ 2582. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the learned Courts below have rightly awarded the sentence against the petitioner.
